fatal_errors: The proposed Mo addition to TiVNbTa does not reconstruct the target comparison of CrFeTaVW with Ta-to-Ti-substituted CrFeTiVW.
It omits the target mechanical-alloying, spark-plasma-sintering, and hybrid MD/Monte Carlo atom-swap interventions.
The asserted retention of a single BCC phase, 20–30% strength gain, preserved ductility, and adequate thermal conductivity have no cited supporting evidence.
The experiment does not directly test the proposed dislocation-mobility or creep mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering motivation of strengthening an HEA interlayer at elevated temperature and correctly states the reported TiVNbTa mechanical baseline. Its composition series, undoped control, high-temperature mechanical tests, phase characterization, and thermal measurements could test the main performance claim. However, it is scientifically disconnected from the hidden study, which concerns CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW, hybrid MD/MC segregation predictions, mechanical alloying, SPS phase evolution, and thermal diffusivity from 300 to 1000 K. The proposed Mo mechanism is generic and unsupported by the supplied HEA evidence; the cited Mo-bearing alloys do not establish that dilute Mo will preserve single-phase TiVNbTa, ductility, or thermal transport. Moreover, XRD/SEM evidence of phase purity cannot by itself falsify the claimed lattice-distortion-mediated suppression of dislocation motion and creep; direct creep testing and defect-scale measurements would be required.
